realTask.note: Hero names the task: audit your own router and close the openings nobody chose. Startable today with owned equipment.

activate.note: Checklist recalls only prior-page material (listener inventory, dated baseline, translation vs permission) plus router admin access. No new content smuggled in.

demonstrate.note: One worked example router walked end to end: four findings, each to keep/close/unknown with the reasoning. Repeatable: a reader could apply the same verdict rules.

apply.note: Seven ordered steps on the reader's own router plus fill-in fields for their own findings, verdicts and unknowns. The reader's own data has somewhere to go.

integrate.note: Two-sides proof (router lists + own cellular attempt), changes join the dated baseline, and the next-page pressure is the lab boundary.

questions.teachesOrExplains: The reader leaves having done an audit, not having read about audits. The exercise transfers the closed-boundary vs live-listener distinction.
questions.coreModel: Every finding gets a name and a reason; the proof section refuses to call anything closed from one side.
questions.scope: Read first, change one thing at a time, record each change. Own router or explicit owner okay only; third-party scanners and deliberate exposures excluded with reasons.
